source.title: Information-seeking, curiosity, and attention: computational and neural mechanisms

confidence_rationale: Foundational cross-disciplinary (machine-learning + neuroscience) grounding for the design decision that an information-seeking/curiosity drive is a legitimate, uniform bias that guides exploration -- exactly SD-025's move. It licenses the family of mechanisms SD-025 sits in (automatic novelty bias through learning-progress/information-gain search). Held at 0.68 because it is a design_decision grounding, not an empirical validation, and because SD-025's specific operationalization (density-of-RBF-centers as the information proxy, novelty = density * (1 - familiarity)) is only one member of the family the review surveys -- the review does not endorse density-of-representation specifically.
failure_signatures: The review's stronger mechanisms are learning-progress / information-gain based (seek where you can reduce uncertainty fastest); SD-025's density-following proxy is closer to the 'automatic novelty bias' end and does not explicitly compute expected information gain -- so a strict reading pressures SD-025 toward the weaker/simpler member of the family.

Curiosity-as-density can perseverate on high-density-but-fully-learned regions; the review notes pure novelty biases get 'trapped' without a learning-progress term -- SD-025 mitigates this only via the familiarity EMA, an ad hoc discount rather than a learning-progress signal.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Exploration and information-gathering are guided by a family of mechanisms ranging from automatic biases toward novelty/surprise to systematic searches for learning progress and information gain (curiosity-driven behaviour). These mechanisms are shared across machine learning, active visual sampling, and psychology/neuroscience of curiosity, and can be studied as intrinsic drives that bias action selection independently of extrinsic reward.
mapping.ree_translation: Licenses SD-025's core design decision: adding a uniform, extrinsic-reward-independent information-seeking bias to hippocampal CEM trajectory scoring is a principled instantiation of a well-attested drive, not an ad hoc bonus. SD-025's uniform 'do the same computation everywhere' curiosity term, with approach emerging because DA-expanded (SD-024) regions carry more representational structure, is a concrete member of the novelty/information-bias family the review formalizes.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The review grounds the EXISTENCE and legitimacy of an information-seeking drive, and situates SD-025 in the mechanism family -- but it does not endorse SD-025's specific proxy (representational density in an RBF map) as the information measure, and its strongest mechanisms are learning-progress-based rather than novelty-density-based. So it supports the design DECISION more than the specific FUNCTIONAL FORM. Theory/computational review, not empirical validation.
mapping.source_context: Cross-disciplinary review spanning reinforcement-learning intrinsic motivation, active oculomotor sampling in natural behaviour, and psychology/neuroscience of curiosity; primate/human and machine-learning models.

confidence_components.notes: High-quality, highly-cited review from a strong venue and precisely the right domain-bridge (ML intrinsic motivation <-> neuroscience curiosity). Mapping fidelity moderate: grounds the drive and the family, not SD-025's density-specific form. Transfer risk low-moderate -- the review is explicitly framed as design-relevant computational principles, which is how REE uses it.
